briefing.cue01:
Attention, Commander.
This is Mission Control.
briefing.cue02: Welcome to the Space Mission Program.
briefing.cue03:
Today you are taking command of a mission
that will push the boundaries of human exploration,
briefing.cue04: but reaching space is no simple task.
briefing.cue05:
Every decision matters.
Every resource counts.
briefing.cue06:
And one mistake could put
the entire mission at risk.
briefing.cue08:
Prepare your spacecraft,
coordinate the launch,
briefing.cue10: Your crew is counting on you.
briefing.cue11: The future of this mission is in your hands.

guide.title: CREW GUIDE
guide.hint: Find {name}; the golden ring marks your guide. Press E to talk.
guide.complete.title: Crew briefing complete
guide.complete.task: Visit a yellow Launch or Rover console to prepare and start a mission. Follow the station steps on screen.
guide.complete.hint: The two yellow mission consoles are in the center of the room.
guide.vega.task: Begin with a measurable mission objective. Visit the Objectives station and decide what question your mission will answer.
guide.sol.task: Choose the evidence you need. Visit the Rover Science station to plan the scientific payload and target.
guide.rios.task: Check the engineering choices. Visit the Rover Mobility and Power stations, then review systems and communications.
guide.kade.task: Before you start, review mission readiness, safety, and operations at the Testing or Flight Review station.
crew.kade.text: A launch window is more than a time on the clock. Check upper-level winds and lightning risks before choosing when to go. If conditions fall outside your limits, hold the launch.
crew.rios.text: A heavier payload leaves less room in your mass budget. Track mass and power margins as the design evolves. Test power, communications, and guidance together before declaring the vehicle ready.
crew.sol.text: Choose samples that can answer your mission question. Match your instruments to the material you expect to study, and leave enough time and power to analyze and transmit the results.
crew.vega.text: Start by defining one measurable mission objective. Set clear go/no-go criteria and decide who makes the final call. Protect time and budget for testing and contingencies.
door.stepBack: Step away from the doorway before closing it.
home.controlsHelp: Use WASD or the arrow keys to move. Press E near a crew member or console to interact, and Esc to pause. On touchscreens, use the on-screen controls.

lesson.architecture.text: Plan four connected segments: launch, space, ground, and users. Define how each one contributes to the mission objectives.
lesson.architecture.title: MISSION ARCHITECTURE
lesson.design.text: Compare feasible concepts, select instruments, estimate mass and power, plan communications, and outline the mission.
lesson.design.title: PRELIMINARY DESIGN
lesson.ground.text: Prepare Mission Control, communications, tracking, contingency procedures, launch criteria, and operating schedules.
lesson.ground.title: GROUND OPERATIONS
lesson.launch.text: Prepare and carry out a rocket launch. Consider the launch window, vehicle readiness, ground systems, and flight safety.
lesson.launch.title: ROCKET LAUNCH MISSION
lesson.objectives.text: Begin with a scientific question. Define measurable goals, criteria for success, and the data you need to answer that question.
lesson.objectives.title: MISSION OBJECTIVES
lesson.operations.text: Operate the spacecraft or rover, collect scientific data, monitor system health, evaluate results, and plan the end of the mission.
lesson.operations.title: MISSION OPERATIONS
lesson.requirements.text: Translate mission objectives into verifiable requirements for performance, safety, cost, schedule, and operations. Identify constraints and major risks.
lesson.requirements.title: MISSION REQUIREMENTS
lesson.rover.text: Plan a rover mission to the Moon. Consider payload, communications, mobility on the lunar surface, power, and scientific objectives.
lesson.rover.title: LUNAR ROVER MISSION
lesson.systems.text: Integrate propulsion, power, guidance, software, thermal control, communications, and ground operations into a single verified system.
lesson.systems.title: SYSTEMS ENGINEERING
lesson.testing.text: Build and integrate subsystems, verify the requirements, run environmental tests, and complete flight readiness reviews before launch.
lesson.testing.title: TESTING AND FLIGHT READINESS

station.trade.battery.grande: Long endurance at a higher mass and budget cost.
station.trade.battery.media: Reasonable endurance for a route with stops.
station.trade.battery.pequena: Light, but needs solar charging between tasks.
station.trade.camera.basica: Minimal power draw. Each data packet is worth its standard value.
station.trade.camera.hd: Each transmission is worth 50% more, but the camera constantly draws more power.
station.trade.chassis.estandar: A balance of speed, energy use and durability.
station.trade.chassis.ligero: Fast and efficient, but unarmored. Collisions use more energy.
station.trade.chassis.reforzado: Endures collisions, but is slow, heavy and draws more energy when moving.
station.trade.comms.alta: Fast, efficient transmission at a high mass and price.
station.trade.comms.baja: Cheap, but sends slowly and uses more energy.
station.trade.comms.media: A balance of time, energy and mass.
station.trade.instrument.laser: Fast analysis with good science value at a higher price.
station.trade.instrument.taladro: Higher science value per sample, but slower and more energy intensive.
station.trade.solar.avanzado: Fast charging lets you use a smaller battery.
station.trade.solar.basico: Slow to recharge. Works best with a large battery.
station.trade.solar.medio: Useful charging during analysis and transmissions.
station.trade.wheels.estandar: A neutral choice for most terrain.
station.trade.wheels.ligeras: Cheap and fast, but more vulnerable to collisions.
station.trade.wheels.todoterreno: Halves collision damage at the cost of extra mass and power draw.
